user.text: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.

history.assistant:

Product links slide forward, the back link slides in the opposite direction, and Suspense skeletons hand off smoothly to content. Reduced-motion settings disable these animations and the skeleton pulse.

Upgraded React and React DOM to 19.3.0, which provides ViewTransition. Verification passed: npm run build, npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false, and git diff --check all exited 0. I did not verify the animations visually in a browser.

288	The CSS for directional slides:
289	
290	```css filename="app/globals.css"
291	::view-transition-old(.nav-forward) {
292	  --slide-offset: -60px;
293	  animation:
294	    150ms ease-in both fade reverse,
295	    400ms ease-in-out both slide reverse;
296	}
297	::view-transition-new(.nav-forward) {
298	  --slide-offset: 60px;
299	  animation:
300	    210ms ease-out 150ms both fade,
301	    400ms ease-in-out both slide;
302	}
303	
304	::view-transition-old(.nav-back) {
305	  --slide-offset: 60px;
306	  animation:
307	    150ms ease-in both fade reverse,
308	    400ms ease-in-out both slide reverse;
309	}
310	::view-transition-new(.nav-back) {
311	  --slide-offset: -60px;
312	  animation:
313	    210ms ease-out 150ms both fade,
314	    400ms ease-in-out both slide;
315	}
316	
317	@keyframes slide {
318	  from {
319	    translate: var(--slide-offset);
320	  }
321	  to {
322	    translate: 0;
323	  }
324	}
325	```
326	
327	The 60px offset is enough to communicate direction without making the user track a fast-moving element across the screen.
328	
329	#### Anchoring the header
330	
331	During directional slides, the header should not move. A sliding header breaks the user's spatial anchor. They need one fixed reference point to understand that the _content_ moved, not the entire viewport.
332	
333	Assign the header a `viewTransitionName` and suppress its animation in CSS:
334	
335	```tsx filename="components/header.tsx"
336	<header style={{ viewTransitionName: 'site-header' }}>
337	  {/* navigation links */}
338	</header>
339	```
340	
341	```css filename="app/globals.css"
342	::view-transition-group(site-header) {
343	  animation: none;
344	  z-index: 100;
345	}
346	::view-transition-old(site-header) {
347	  display: none;
348	}
349	::view-transition-new(site-header) {
350	  animation: none;
351	}
352	```
353	
354	The `display: none` on the old snapshot prevents a flash where both old and new headers are briefly visible. The `z-index: 100` ensures the header renders above the sliding content.
355	
356	If we navigate forward to a photo, content slides left. If we click the "← Gallery" link (tagged with `nav-back`), content slides right. The header stays fixed throughout both transitions.
357	
358	Browser-initiated back navigations (the back button or swipe gestures) do not carry a transition type, so the directional slide does not play. The shared element morph from Step 1 still applies if both pages have matching `name` props.
359	
360	#### Keeping the page interactive
361	
362	While a transition runs, the `::view-transition` overlay captures pointer events, so clicks during the animation are lost. Let them pass through to the live page:
363	
364	```css filename="app/globals.css"
365	::view-transition {
366	  pointer-events: none;
367	}
368	```
369	
370	This restores interactivity for unnamed content. Hit-testing still skips named participants (like the anchored header) for the transition's duration, so keep transitions short and avoid naming elements the user clicks rapidly.
371	
372	#### Respecting reduced motion
373	
374	Directional slides simulate physical movement across the viewport. This is the most common trigger for motion sensitivity. Morphs, reveals, and crossfades carry less risk since they affect smaller areas or rely on opacity rather than position.
375	
376	The simplest approach is to disable all animation durations:
377	
378	```css filename="app/globals.css"
379	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
380	  ::view-transition-old(*),
381	  ::view-transition-new(*),
382	  ::view-transition-group(*) {
383	    animation-duration: 0s !important;
384	    animation-delay: 0s !important;
385	  }
386	}
387	```
388	
389	Without animation, content swaps instantly, which is the browser's default behavior. A more refined approach would preserve crossfades and opacity transitions while removing positional movement. See ["No Motion Isn't Always prefers-reduced-motion"](https://css-tricks.com/nuking-motion-with-prefers-reduced-motion/) for more on this.
390	
391	### Step 4: Crossfade content within the same route
392	
393	The gallery has a photographer section with tabs. Each tab shows a different photographer's photos, but the route structure is the same: `/collection/[slug]`. Clicking between tabs does not feel like navigating to a new page. It feels like switching content within the same container.
394	
395	A directional slide would be wrong here. Slides communicate "going to a new place." A crossfade communicates "same place, different content." The container persists (continuity), only the grid inside changes (swap).
396	
397	Use a `ViewTransition` with `key` set to the current slug. When the key changes, React triggers a transition between the old and new content:
398	
399	```tsx filename="app/collection/[slug]/page.tsx"
400	import { Suspense, ViewTransition } from 'react'
401	
402	export default async function CollectionPage({ params }) {
403	  const { slug } = await params
404	
405	  return (
406	    <Suspense fallback={<CollectionGridSkeleton />}>
407	      <ViewTransition
408	        key={slug}
409	        name="collection-content"
410	        share="auto"
411	        enter="auto"
412	        default="none"
413	      >
414	        <CollectionGrid slug={slug} />
415	      </ViewTransition>
416	    </Suspense>
417	  )
418	}
419	```
420	
421	The `share="auto"` and `enter="auto"` props tell React to use its default crossfade animation. The `name` prop gives the container an identity so React knows what to animate. The navigation triggers the transition; the `key={slug}` change makes React treat the old and new content as an exit/enter pair (activating `share`) instead of an in-place update.
422	
423	If we click between photographer tabs, the grid crossfades. The tab bar and surrounding layout do not move. Only the photo grid transitions between states.
424	
425	## Next steps
426	
427	You now know how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation. Shared elements communicate continuity across routes. Suspense reveals animate loading handoffs. Directional slides encode navigation history. Crossfades signal content changes within the same location.
428	
429	Each pattern answers a different question for the user:
430	
431	| Pattern                | What it communicates            |
432	| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
433	| Shared element (morph) | "Same thing, going deeper"      |
434	| Suspense reveal        | "Data loaded"                   |
435	| Directional slide      | "Going forward / coming back"   |
436	| Same-route crossfade   | "Same place, different content" |
437

441	- [`useRouter`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), which also supports `transitionTypes` in `push()` and `replace()`
442	- [React `ViewTransition` component](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)
